stories.headline: The United States will host the first Women's Club World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA has confirmed that the United States will host the first Women's Club World Cup. The tournament is scheduled to run from 5 to 30 January 2028, and 19 teams will contest it. It was originally planned for early 2026, but was delayed by two years.

stories.headline: The Sakharov Prize goes to the International Criminal Court
stories.summary: The European Parliament has awarded its 2026 Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and its officials, for their work in global justice and upholding international law. The prize is named after the Russian scientist and dissident Andrei Sakharov, and was established in December 1988. It carries a monetary award of €50,000.

stories.headline: Finland licences the world's first store for spent nuclear fuel
stories.summary: Finland's government has granted the company Posiva an operating licence for Onkalo, a repository at Eurajoki on the country's west coast. It is the world's first licensed deep geological disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel. The store is being dug into granite bedrock about five kilometres from the Olkiluoto power plants.

stories.headline: Honey bees crowd out wild pollinators around Cambridge
stories.summary: Researchers at Anglia Ruskin University watched pollinators for two years at five sites in and around Cambridge. On bramble, doubling the density of honey bees went with a 14% fall in bumblebee numbers. The ivy bee, first documented in Britain in 2001, was the only pollinator seen to challenge the honey bees.
